title: Momentum-dependent precessional and nutational spin pumping in a honeycomb antiferromagnet
authors: Suman Mukherjee, Subhadip Ghosh, Ritwik Mondal
abstract: The ultrafast magnetic inertial dynamics on subpicosecond timescales generate an additional high-frequency terahertz nutational resonance. Here, we investigate momentum-resolved spin pumping in a two-dimensional honeycomb antiferromagnet by incorporating spin inertia into the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation. Using a microscopic two-sublattice model with $J_1$-$J_2$-$J_3$ exchange interactions, we calculate the precessional and nutational magnon spectra and their corresponding intra- and inter-sublattice spin pumping contributions throughout the Brillouin zone. For parameters representative of MnPS$_3$, we find a pronounced complementary momentum dependence of the two spin pumping channels: the precessional current is strongly suppressed around the $Γ$ point ($0.01\%$) and increases towards the Brillouin zone boundary ($100\%$ at $K$ and $87\%$ at $M$), whereas the nutational current is largest near $Γ$ ($100\%$) and decreases towards the boundary ($68\%$ at $K$ and $69\%$ at $M$). This contrasting momentum dependence provides a means of distinguishing spin nutation from conventional precessional motion. We further demonstrate that the nutational spin pumping current is strongly controlled by the inertial relaxation time $η$, in contrast to the comparatively weak $η$ dependence of the precessional current. In the small-$η$ regime, our analytical results show that the intra-sublattice nutational spin pumping current exhibits a leading-order dependence of $1/η^3$. The spin pumping response can also be tuned through the exchange interaction strengths and magnetic moment. Our further results on the magnetic field dependence of spin pumping reveal that the ratio of nutational spin pumping current increases with magnetic field strength, whereas the corresponding precessional counterpart decreases.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes spin pumping in a honeycomb antiferromagnet by incorporating magnetic inertia, leading to the emergence of nutational dynamics alongside conventional precession. The key finding is the contrasting momentum dependence of these two spin pumping channels, which can be used to experimentally separate them. The results also show that the nutational response is highly sensitive to the inertial relaxation time.
main_problem: The study investigates the momentum-dependent precessional and nutational spin pumping in a two-dimensional honeycomb antiferromagnet.
main_result: The precessional and nutational spin pumping currents exhibit contrasting momentum dependencies across the Brillouin zone, allowing for their experimental distinction. Furthermore, the nutational current is strongly controlled by the inertial relaxation time, while the ratio of nutational to precessional current increases with the applied magnetic field.
method: The authors used a microscopic two-sublattice model incorporating spin inertia into the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation to calculate the magnon spectra and spin pumping contributions.
model_or_system: The system is a 2D honeycomb antiferromagnet, modeled using a two-sublattice approach with $J_1$-$J_2$-$J_3$ exchange interactions, and dynamics are governed by the inertial LLG equation.
key_observables: Precessional and nutational spin pumping currents, their momentum dependence across the Brillouin zone ($\Gamma$ to $K$ to $M$), and the ratio of these currents under varying fields.
important_parameters: Inertial relaxation time ($\eta$), exchange interaction strengths ($J_i$), and the strength of the static magnetic field ($\mathbf{B}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis uses a linearized inertial LLG equation and assumes the equilibrium magnetization is oriented out of the plane.
figures_summary: Figures likely show color maps of the normalized precessional and nutational spin pumping currents across the Brillouin zone, illustrating their distinct momentum profiles.
paper_structure: The paper builds upon previous work by extending the analysis of spin pumping from uniform ($\Gamma$ point) dynamics to map the currents across the entire Brillouin zone, detailing the role of spin inertia and external magnetic fields.
why_interesting: The explicit inclusion of magnetic inertia leading to nutational dynamics, combined with momentum-resolved spin pumping calculations, provides a sophisticated theoretical tool to distinguish between different types of magnetic excitations in complex quantum magnets.
